description: A wavetable voice whose table is built by hand: six controls sculpt one shape, and each snap stores that shape into a table of eight, which the oscillator then scans through

params.text: Sets how many peaks the sculpted shape has, 1 to 8
Tilts the sculpted shape toward one side, -100 to 100 per cent
Bends the sculpted shape's segments between logarithmic and exponential, -100 to 100 per cent
Leans the sculpted shape's peaks forward or back, -100 to 100 per cent
Sets how wide the peaks of the sculpted shape are
Folds the sculpted shape back on itself, adding harmonics
Adds a slow random movement of its own to every shape control, so the sculpted shape evolves with no CV patched
Sets how fast the playback scans through the stored shapes: positive from oldest to newest, negative the other way, and at the centre detent the position is locked
Sets how long a change of scan speed takes to arrive, from instant to five seconds
Stores the sculpted shape into the table on each press, writing over the oldest of the eight when the table is full

inputs.text: Sets the pitch as a volt per octave
Adds to the frequency directly, about 100Hz per volt, rather than by octaves
A rise restarts the wave at the beginning of its cycle
Changes the scan speed, ±5V for the whole travel, added to the velocity knob
A rise stores the sculpted shape into the table
A rise jumps the scan position to the oldest stored shape
Changes the amount of internal random movement, added to the wander knob
Changes how many peaks the sculpted shape has, added to the peaks knob
Changes the tilt of the sculpted shape, added to the bias knob
Changes the segment curve of the sculpted shape, added to the transition knob
Changes the lean of the sculpted shape's peaks, added to the skew knob
Changes how wide the peaks are, added to the width knob
Changes the folding, added to the fold knob

outputs.text: The oscillator, reading the stored shapes rather than the one being sculpted

notes: the module is silent until a shape has been snapped: the six sculpting controls shape a wave that is only drawn on the display, and the output reads the stored table
the table holds eight shapes and is written oldest first, so the ninth snap writes over the first
every stored shape is pre-rendered as a band-limited set of tables, so playback does not alias however high the pitch is
menu: Snap now — stores the sculpted shape into the table, the same action as the panel button
Clear all snapshots — empties the table, which leaves the module silent again
